scope: Production API-reference route bundle budget and local HTTPS browser-load observations. Single-run development measurements; not service-capacity or production-SLO evidence.

environment.application: Rust debug server behind the local HTTPS test proxy; SvelteKit production build
environment.database: Disposable Percona Distribution for PostgreSQL container
environment.cacheSequence: One fresh browser context for the cold navigation, followed by a reload in the same context for the warm navigation. No page request interception was enabled during the measurement because Playwright routing disables the browser HTTP cache.

routeBundle.includes: The API-reference route entry, its eagerly imported JavaScript dependencies and route CSS, counted once from the SvelteKit build manifest.
routeBundle.excludes: Shared application chunks, separately fetched OpenAPI JSON, and content already held in the browser cache.

verification.assetBudget: make build-web passed; the deterministic build-manifest check enforces the 80 KiB gzip ceiling.
verification.browserSuite: make test-browser-focused passed, including cold/warm transfer comparison, response cache headers, no reference assets on the ordinary login page, API-reference navigation, accessibility names and landmarks, documented interactions, signed-out behavior, Spanish presentation, cookie omission, and mobile/zoom bounds.
verification.schemaExamples: make api-spec-check passed with source-defined schema validation and bundled-copy parity checks.
verification.unitChecks: make check passed, including the schema validator and asset-budget unit tests.

limitations: Cold and warm figures are single-run observations on one local development host. They are not stable timing benchmarks or capacity promises.
The route budget is a reproducible artifact-size gate; browser timings may vary with hardware, browser version, load, and TLS state.

The contract checker validates the schema assertion vocabulary currently used by this API contract; it is not a complete OpenAPI or JSON Schema implementation, and it does not prove exact parity with every Rust handler.
Manual screen-reader review and full mechanical Rust-handler/schema parity remain open work for issue #43.
